items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the exemption of certain parcels of land
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6884

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the
exemption of certain parcels of land

 PURPOSE :

To add certain parcels of land in the City of Peekskill to the list of
premises which are exempt from the provisions of law which generally
restrict manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers from sharing an
interest in a liquor license.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Amends Sections 101(1)(a) and 106(13) of the Alcoholic Beverage
Control Law, which restrict the relationships between manufacturers,
wholesalers and retailers, by adding a specific parcel of land in the
City of Peekskill to the list of parcels which are exempt from these
laws.

 EXISTING LAW :

Current law restricts ownership interests between alcohol
manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers. However, the law has been
amended on occasion to create specific exemptions from these general
prohibitions for specific parcels of land.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill seeks to assist the economic revitalization of the City of
Peekskill by enabling the reopening of the Charles Point Marina, which
has operated as a restaurant, catering hall and Distillery. The
Charles Point Marina was an important part of the cultural life of the
City of Peekskill, and its revitalization will provide an economic
boost and vitality to the area.

Unfortunately, almost all of the business at the Charles Point Marina
have left in the last few years. It was sold in 2014 to Diamond
Properties, a business in which two of the partners are successfully
operating bowling alley/amusement centers and restaurants throughout
Westchester County. Given their track record, there is excitement
about the rebirth of the Marina. However, an obstacle arose when it
was learned that the provisions of the ABC Law would restrict the
ability to open a small brewery onsite as well as resurrect the
distillery at the historic distillery building.

Since the 1930s, when Prohibition was repealed, New York State law has
restricted owners of alcohol manufacturer's licenses, wholesale
licenses and retail licenses from having an interest in each other.
Efforts have been underway to propose a comprehensive update of the
Alcoholic Beverage Control Law, and these types of ownership issues
will likely be evaluated as part of any such review.

In the meantime, this bill creates a limited exception to allow
manufacturing tenants in the Marina building, whose owners are holders
of a retail licenses in NYS. The Alcoholic Beverage Control Law has
previously been amended to create a specific, limited exemptions from
the "tied house" restrictions. This bill would create a similar
exemption in recognition of the economic value of the Charles Point
Marina re-development would have to the city of Peekskill.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.
 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

The affected parcel has previously been an important economic
contributor to the City of Peekskill, and will help generate sales tax
and property tax revenues for the City and County of Westchester.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately

summary: Adds certain parcels of land in the city of Peekskill and in the town of Greenburgh to the list of premises which are exempt from the provisions of law which restrict manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers from sharing an interest in a liquor license.
